messages:
Evan Park: Heads up — after the gpu-operator roll in us-west-2 at 03:10UTC we started seeing a pile of GPU pods stuck Pending. Node allocatable shows 0 GPUs even though capacity is 8 on the instances.

Evan Park: quick snippet from one node:```$ kubectl describe node ip-10-0-2-15\nCapacity:\n  nvidia.com/gpu: 8\nAllocatable:\n  nvidia.com/gpu: 0\nNon-terminated Pods: 42\n```

Priya Sharma: Oof. Did the device-plugin register? `kubectl get pods -n gpu-operator` looks healthy?

Evan Park: device-plugin DaemonSet is Running, logs show it registered but there are warnings about resource name mismatch: `resourceName: nvidia.com/gpu-0` in logs for a bit, then it re-registered as `nvidia.com/gpu`. Not sure which timing aligned with the rollout.

Liam O'Connor: We saw a config change in the operator chart — the new image sets the plugin to advertise device IDs instead of aggregated count to support MIG. That changes the initial registration handshake with kubelet, and kubelet's allocatable gets set to 0 until a full re-register completes. Symptoms line up. :facepalm:

Jordan Kim: Confirmed on one node — when I forced a kubelet restart the device plugin re-registers and allocatable jumps back to 8. So the underlying devices are fine. It's a timing/registration race introduced by the new plugin behaviour.

Priya Sharma: Is this just us-west-2 or across clusters?

Evan Park: Primarily us-west-2 and a couple of dev fleets that pulled the chart auto-upgrade. eu-central hasn't flipped.

Liam O'Connor: Risks: any scale-up during the race will schedule pods onto nodes that kube-scheduler considers unschedulable -> backpressure / queue buildup. Also impacts autoscaler decisions.

Priya Sharma: Short-term mitigation — rolling restart of kubelets on affected nodes? That's noisy. Better: revert the chart to the previous operator image that advertised aggregated counts.

Jordan Kim: I pushed an emergency PR to the chart repo to pin the gpu-operator image to v1.5.3 and disable the `advertise-device-ids` flag. Rolling back now on us-west-2 staging first.

deploy-bot: deploy started by Jordan Kim — chart/gpu-operator pinned to v1.5.3 on cluster us-west-2-staging (rollout id: r-20260318-01).

Evan Park: If rollback is quick we should be fine. Action items: Jordan to complete rollback to prod, Liam to run a node-level script to restart kubelets in controlled batches for any nodes that stayed with allocatable 0, Priya to throttle auto-upgrades in the chart repo.

Liam O'Connor: I'll run a `kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.allocatable.nvidia.com/gpu}\n{end}'` pass and target restarts for nodes with allocatable==0. Using 5-node batches with 5m wait between.

Priya Sharma: Also creating an alert: if allocatable GPUs on a node < capacity for >2m, page oncall. Will add note to runbook about this plugin behaviour and kubelet restart workaround.

Evan Park: Long-term: we need an integration test in our upgrade pipeline that does operator -> device-plugin handshake checks, and ensure autoscaler respects transient 0 allocatable state. Also flag to operator chart maintainers to make device-id advertisement opt-in.

Jordan Kim: Agreed. I'll open a GH issue linking logs and the chart diff. Will also capture a small reproducer to hand to the upstream operator maintainers.

Priya Sharma: Thanks team. If anyone sees any new Pending GPU pods ping here with pod name + node. :thumbsup:
